defect.evidence_quote: the inevitable-discovery exception to the exclusionary rule does not apply, and the gun discovered during the illegal search of the backpack must be suppressed.
defect.problem: The proposition is supportable in substance but the holding field is truncated with an ellipsis and omits the actual disposition/holding on inevitable discovery.
defect.proposed_fix: Replace with a complete holding: the government conceded the backpack search was not a valid search incident to arrest, invoked inevitable discovery, and the Tenth Circuit held the government failed to prove lawful impoundment/inventory and ordered suppression.

reasons: Opinion text supports the concession and inevitable-discovery theory.
The same opinion text supplies the missing outcome: inevitable discovery did not apply and the gun had to be suppressed.
residual_risks: No separate lake holding field beyond page text was available; support comes from the cached opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: State the full holding rather than ending after then relied on.

defect.evidence_quote: Instead, this case turns on whether the officers would have validly impounded Braxton’s backpack in the absence of the illegal search incident to arrest.
defect.problem: Inventory Searches is supportable only as a secondary home. The opinion says the inventory-search point itself was not disputed and that the case turned on lawful impoundment/community caretaking, so the role should not imply an affirmative inventory-search holding.
defect.proposed_fix: Tighten the role to a secondary/limiting inventory-search entry, e.g. inventory-search theory via inevitable discovery failed because lawful impoundment was not proven; consider adding or prioritizing Community Caretaking or Inevitable Discovery.

reasons: The opinion discusses inventory search as part of the government's inevitable-discovery theory.
But the court expressly made valid impoundment, not inventory-search procedure, the decisive point.
residual_risks: content_page.md frontmatter lists Inventory Searches, while the visible Appears on section lists Special Needs and Administrative Searches.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Mark as secondary and specify the impoundment prerequisite to any inventory-search theory.
